tables.caption: The mature amino acid sequences of peptide SS1 and its analogues.
footnotes: The amino acid with a grey and ‘--’ mark was deleted amino acid at that position. The amino acid with a green mark was changed from Alanine (A) to Valine (V). The amino acid with a yellow mark was changed from Alanine (A) to Glycine (G). The amino acid with a pink colour was changed from Serine (S) to Lysine (K).

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: The physicochemical parameters of peptide SS1 and its analogues.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: Antimicrobial activity of SS1 and its analogues against various microorganisms.

tables.label: Table 4
tables.caption: HC50, GM, and TI values of SS1 and its analogues.
footnotes: a HC50 was the minimum haemolytic concentration that caused 50% haemolysis of hRBCs. b The geometric mean (GM) of peptides against microorganisms was calculated using MICs. The formula was GMMIC = MIC1·MIC2⋯MICnn (n: the number of the MIC value of the peptide). The MICs of bacteria were obtained from Table 3 to calculate the GM value. c The therapeutic index (TI) is a ratio that compares the blood concentration at which a drug becomes toxic and the concentration at which the drug is effective. TI values were calculated as HC50/GMMIC. Larger values indicated greater cell selectivity. When no detectable antimicrobial activity was observed at 128.00 μM, a value of 256.00 μM was utilized to calculate the TI value.
